reuse.why: The actions share category selection and reuse existing budget, sheet, batching and undo helpers, although copyPreviousMonth retains its own income eligibility check.

duplication.why: Repeated category queries and iteration are consolidated, but the income exclusion remains duplicated between copyPreviousMonth and forEachMonthWideCategory.

placement.why: Selection policy and budget calculations remain in budget/actions.ts, while method registration and undo integration follow app.ts conventions.

scope.why: The changes are confined to the requested month-wide actions, their method registration and focused tests.

maintainability.why: The shared selector and argument type make future exclusion changes straightforward, with a minor maintenance risk from keeping income eligibility in two places.

bypasses_abstraction.where: copyPreviousMonth uses getMonthWideCategories directly and repeats the income guard instead of using forEachMonthWideCategory.

disguised_duplication.where: The remaining duplicated income guard is explicit; the repeated category-selection queries are actually consolidated.

abstraction_drift.where: The shared selection gains the includeHidden option and its conditional SQL override; copyPreviousMonth bypasses the shared iterator and separately enforces income eligibility.
